title: Decoding first, comprehension by listening
statement: For learners who can't yet decode, spend reading time on decoding and fluency and build comprehension by listening, since reading comprehension is decoding times language comprehension.
example: One grade-1 plan set the typical reader's 60 words correct per minute against a threshold of 90, below which comprehension is very difficult.
detail: A pedagogy red team on a second-grade plan applied the Simple View of Reading: reading comprehension is decoding times language comprehension, so when decoding is near zero, comprehension-item instruction multiplies against a near-zero factor and yields near-zero transfer (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/redteam-2-pedagogy.md`, line 34). It called decode-first the correct sequence and fluency the mechanism that frees working memory for comprehension (the same file, lines 28 and 60). A grade-1 plan set the typical grade-1 rate of 60 words correct per minute against a threshold of 90 below which comprehension is very difficult, and concluded that its comprehension course must be led by oral language and listening comprehension, not cold text, and must size its claims to the learners decoding doesn't hold back (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g1-reading/brainlifts/v0.1.md`, line 40).
against: The grade-1 plan flags its own fluency targets as unreconciled across its references (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g1-reading/brainlifts/v0.1.md`, line 30), and it keeps audio off the scored check, so listening carries the teaching while the scored reading stays in print (the same file, line 43).

evidence.quote: Reading Comprehension = Decoding × Language Comprehension. It is a *product*, not a sum. When decoding ≈ 0, the product ≈ 0 **regardless of language comprehension**.
Adding comprehension-item instruction multiplies against a near-zero decoding factor and yields near-zero transfer.
Fluency is not a "strength to coast on"; it is the *mechanism* by which decoding stops consuming working memory so that comprehension becomes possible.
Comprehension is *"very difficult below 90 words correct per minute"*
but the G1 norm is only **60 WCPM**
so much of the typical G1 cohort sits *below the fluency at which cold-text comprehension instruction is even effective*
Consequence: a G1 comprehension course must be **oral-language / listening-comprehension-led**, not cold-text-led, and **size its MAP-reach claim to the non-decoding-gated fraction**.
Audio supports learning; it never reads the scored item aloud.

citations.ref: Decoding, Reading, and Reading Disability, Remedial and Special Education 7(1) (1986)
The simple view of reading, Reading and Writing 2 (1990)
